# Docket

Docket is a read-only HTTP API that publishes what it observed about ERC-8004 agents
registered on BNB Smart Chain: what each agent declares about itself, and whether the
endpoint it declared answered when Docket asked.

Docket does not rate, endorse, or vouch for any agent. Read "Observations, not
endorsements" at the bottom of this file before you quote anything from it.


## Base URL

The origin this file was served from. Every path below is relative to it. There is no
public deployment yet; the local default is http://127.0.0.1:8099

    DOCKET=http://127.0.0.1:8099

Started with:

    python -m uvicorn --factory "docket.api:create_app" --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8099

No authentication, no API key, no rate limit. Only GET is served. Nothing here writes,
sweeps, or probes anything, so a caller cannot change what Docket has observed by
calling it. Responses are JSON except /llms.txt (text/plain) and /skill.md
(text/markdown). CORS: GET from any origin, no credentials.

Docket serves one snapshot at a time. Which one is stated in every response that
carries a number, and at GET /health.


## Endpoints

GET /
    Service identity and the links needed to orient. No parameters.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/"

GET /health
    Docket's own liveness, and the snapshot id it is serving. Returns
    {"status": "ok", "snapshot_id": 3}, or status "no_snapshot" when no sweep has
    been ingested yet. No parameters.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/health"

GET /stats
    Every generated figure for the served snapshot, each one inside the coverage it
    was computed from. No parameters. Fields:

      coverage                 see "Coverage" below; required, never absent
      with_feedback            agents in this snapshot with >= 1 feedback record
      callable_declared        agents declaring an A2A or MCP protocol
      endpoints_resolved       endpoint registration rows read from agent cards, over
                               all kinds (a2a, mcp, web, service). One URL registered
                               under two kinds counts twice: on snapshot 3 this is 78
                               rows over 43 distinct (agent, URL) pairs
      endpoints_probed         endpoints actually probed. Only a2a and mcp are probed
      endpoints_responded      of those probed, how many got an HTTP response
      responded_pct_of_probed  named for its denominator. It is a share of
                               endpoints_probed and of nothing else
      blocked_by_policy        targets Docket refused to contact (see "blocked")
      unresolved               hostnames that would not resolve (see "unresolved")
      distinct_publishers      distinct publisher keys in the snapshot
      top_publishers           the five largest, with counts and share of the snapshot
      probe_method             one line stating how liveness was measured

    curl -s "$DOCKET/stats"

GET /agents
    Filterable listing. All parameters optional; omitting one does not filter on it.

      has_feedback        true|false   agent has >= 1 feedback record
      declares_callable   true|false   agent declares an A2A or MCP protocol. This is
                                       a claim the agent made, not a probe result
      responded           true|false   at least one of the agent's probed endpoints
                                       returned outcome "responded" in this snapshot
      publisher           string       exact match on the publisher key, e.g.
                                       "openodds.ai". The key groups agents minted by
                                       one publisher or family; when an agent has no
                                       usable name it is "owner:0x..."
      limit               int          default 50, clamped into [1, 100]
      offset              int          default 0, negatives clamped to 0

    Returns {"items": [...], "total": N, "limit": L, "offset": O, "coverage": {...}}.
    "total" is the count after filtering and before pagination, so it does not change
    as you page. Each item carries: agent_id, token_id, name, description,
    owner_address, has_feedback, feedback_count, declares_callable, protocols, x402,
    publisher, placeholder_name (true when the name is a registry-generated
    "Agent #123" rather than one the publisher chose).

    curl -s "$DOCKET/agents?declares_callable=true&limit=3"
    curl -s "$DOCKET/agents?responded=true&limit=5"

GET /agents/{agent_id}
    One agent, with its resolved endpoint URLs and every timestamped observation of
    them. agent_id is "{chain_id}:{registry_address}:{token_id}" and contains colons;
    send it literally, do not URL-encode the colons. Adds to the listing fields:

      endpoints      distinct URLs resolved from this agent's card, sorted
      observations   one entry per probed URL: url, kind (the probeable kind the URL
                     was registered under), observed_at, outcome, status_code,
                     elapsed_ms, detail
      coverage       the snapshot this agent was read from

    An agent with no observations was never probed. That is a statement about
    Docket's coverage, not about the agent.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/agents/56:0x8004a169fb4a3325136eb29fa0ceb6d2e539a432:49637"

GET /llms.txt
    This file. text/plain.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/llms.txt"

GET /skill.md
    A drop-in skill file for a coding agent: the same endpoints as a table, plus
    worked examples for the three workflows Docket is actually for. text/markdown.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/skill.md"

GET /openapi.json
    The generated OpenAPI 3.1 schema for every path above. Do not invent endpoints:
    if a workflow is not in this file or that schema, Docket does not serve it.

    curl -s "$DOCKET/openapi.json"


## Errors

Every error, at every status, has the same shape:

    {"error": {"code": "agent_not_found", "message": "what to do about it"}}

Branch on "code", which is stable. "message" is prose for a human and may change.

      agent_not_found          404  no such agent in the served snapshot
      not_found                404  no such path
      method_not_allowed       405  the path exists, that method does not
      invalid_query_parameter  422  message names the offending parameter
      no_snapshot              503  nothing has been ingested yet


## Coverage: why every number carries one

A count without its population is unreadable, so no response that carries a number
omits the coverage it was counted in. Every "coverage" object has:

      snapshot_id   which capture this figure came from
      captured_at   ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of that capture
      sampled       agents actually stored in the snapshot
      expected      agents the registry API said the query would return
      dropped       expected - sampled. Above 0, the snapshot is missing rows and
                    every count in the response understates its population
      complete      true only when sampled == expected and sampled > 0
      filter        which subset of the snapshot this response describes, e.g.
                    "declares_callable=true", or null for the whole snapshot

The population itself is a choice worth stating. BNB Smart Chain carries roughly
247,278 registered ERC-8004 agents, of which 506 (0.205%) have ever received a single
feedback record. The default snapshot covers those 506, not the whole registry,
because a full sweep of 247,278 is not something Docket has done. Any figure below is
a figure about that feedback population.

When you quote a Docket number, quote its coverage with it.


## Liveness outcome vocabulary

The vocabulary is closed. An observation's "outcome" is exactly one of six values.

Method: one GET per declared A2A or MCP endpoint, single attempt, 8s timeout,
redirects not followed, every target vetted by an SSRF guard before any connection is
opened. Single attempt means a failure is one observation at one moment, not a
pattern. Only a2a and mcp endpoints are probed; web and service registrations are
recorded and left alone.

  responded
      A host answered at any HTTP status. status_code carries which.
      Implies: something is listening at that URL and it replied.
      Does NOT imply: the agent does anything useful, is the agent it claims to be,
      or that the response had anything to do with ERC-8004. A 404 counts as
      responded because it proves the host is up. On snapshot 3, one agent's declared
      endpoint is the block explorer's own /create page, which answered 308; another
      declares a public NFT marketplace listing, which answered 200. Both are
      recorded as responded, and neither is evidence of a working agent.

  timeout
      No response within 8s. Implies nothing beyond that one attempt at that moment.

  refused
      The connection was refused. Same caveat: one attempt, one moment.

  error
      The request failed for some other reason; "detail" names the exception type.

  blocked
      Docket refused the target on policy grounds and never opened a connection: a
      non-HTTP scheme, or an address that is private, loopback, or CGNAT. "detail"
      says which.
      Implies: Docket did not probe it, so Docket knows nothing about it.
      Does NOT imply: the agent is dangerous, malicious, or misconfigured. On
      snapshot 3 every blocked target is an "npm://" package reference, which is a
      distribution channel, not a URL a GET can reach.

  unresolved
      DNS did not resolve the hostname, after one retry, so nothing was contacted.
      Implies: that name did not resolve from Docket's network at that moment.
      Does NOT imply: a safety refusal, or that the agent is offline for everyone.
      This is kept separate from "blocked" on purpose. Summing the two would publish
      DNS trouble as a safety statistic.


## Worked example: the honest headline

The shape of every claim Docket makes. Figures below are snapshot 3, captured
2026-08-07T17:51:02Z, sampled 506 of 506 expected, dropped 0, complete true, covering
the population "BSC agents with >= 1 feedback record".

    Of the 506 agents in this snapshot, 31 declare a callable A2A or MCP endpoint.
    Enrichment resolved 78 endpoint registration rows from their cards; 35 of those
    were A2A or MCP and were probed. 13 responded -- 37.143% of the 35 probed. The
    other 22: 11 unresolved, 10 blocked by policy, 1 timed out.

Read what that does and does not say.

  - 37.143% is a share of the 35 endpoints probed. It is not 37% of 506 agents, and
    it is emphatically not 37% of the 247,278 agents on BNB Smart Chain.
  - The 13 responses mean 13 hosts answered. None of them is a working-agent count.
  - The 10 blocked are Docket's own refusals. They are not misconduct findings.
  - 31 of 506 declaring a callable endpoint is a count of claims agents made about
    themselves, not of endpoints that work.
  - Change the snapshot and every number here changes. That is why the snapshot id
    travels with them.

Reproduce it:

    curl -s "$DOCKET/stats"


## Observations, not endorsements

Docket publishes observations. It does not publish verdicts.

No endpoint returns a safety rating, a trust score, a rank, or a recommendation. No
response field is named safe, trusted, verified, recommended, rank, score, or
rating; a test in this repository fails the build if one ever is. Docket lists no
agent as safe, and an agent's presence in any Docket response is not a claim that it
is honest, competent, solvent, or fit for any purpose.

What Docket can tell you: what an agent declared on chain, how much feedback it has
received, whether a host answered its declared endpoint at one moment, and how much
of the registry that observation covers. What it cannot tell you: whether to hire it.
That judgement is the reader's, and Docket is built to hand over the evidence rather
than pre-empt it.
